parsed.stack: Mobile web PWA (SvelteKit/TypeScript) plus email as the actual delivery surface - no app store, no review queue; frontier text model at $0.10/$0.40 per M with each plot's multi-season notes held in flat million-token context at the ~90% cache discount; Postgres + object storage on Fly.io; Resend for the Sunday send; Stripe Checkout direct, no store cut.
milestones: Week 1-2: plot record - beds, what was sown where and when, free-text and photo notes, importable from a photographed notebook page.
Week 3-4: the Sunday generator - one briefing per plot from that plot's own history, with an explicit rule that anything not traceable to the user's own notes gets cut.
Week 5: email delivery, open tracking, and a one-tap 'this line was generic' feedback control feeding a quality score.
Week 6: first-season cold-start mode (a plot with no history gets sowing-window prompts instead of recall, and is told so).
Week 7: Stripe at $4/month after a 4-briefing trial, plus an association pack - a noticeboard PDF and a newsletter paragraph committees can paste.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That four briefings a month built from sparse, misspelled, half-abandoned plot notes read as specifically about this plot rather than as generic seasonal gardening filler, because the entire defensibility claim is recall of the user's own past mistakes.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Get 12 allotment holders to photograph their existing notebooks, generate four weeks of briefings by hand in a chat window, and have each of them mark every line 'about my plot' or 'could be anyone's' - about two days and no code.
